title: Control plane audit mapping and export options with Artemis Systems
meeting_header: Date: 2026-11-06 | Time: 16:00 UTC | Duration: 1:11 | Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Hannah Li (Redwood Product), Priya Kapoor (CISO - Artemis), Ethan Ross (Platform), Lina Park (Compliance), Samir Jain (SRE). Recording: Fireflies auto-transcript. Notes: request for audit mapping, retention policy, KMS integration patterns, export formats (S3/GCP PubSub), and chain-of-custody for admin actions.
summary: Artemis Systems ran through what audit and admin activity Redwood captures natively, discussed live export patterns (S3 + Pub/Sub), retention and immutable snapshots, KMS envelope key flow, and SOC2/ISO artifacts. SE provided architecture sketches and suggested a pilot for 30-day export to Artemis S3 with encrypted at rest keys. Action items include sharing SOC2 pack, sample export manifest, and setting a follow-up pilot kickoff.
topics: what audit events are captured (auth, token ops, model calls, admin UI actions)
export options: nearline S3, streaming Pub/Sub, webhook sink
retention and immutable snapshots for e-discovery
KMS integration: customer-managed CMKs, envelope encryption, key rotation
mapping audit events to Artemis compliance controls
SSO/RBAC: linked principal IDs and session traceability
transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll go ~60 minutes, we have Diego on for the deep bits. Quick intro round?
[00:08] Priya (CISO): Priya here, CISO at Artemis Systems. We're mostly focused on proof of capture for admin activity.
[00:12] Ethan (Platform): Ethan, platform team. We'll handle export endpoints.
[00:16] Diego (Redwood SE): Hi all, Diego from Redwood infra, I did the KMS integration on a recent pilot so I can show patterns.
[00:24] Maya (Redwood AE): Great. Quick agenda: what we capture, how to get it out, retention/immutable snapshot options, and KMS/SSO mapping.
[00:33] Lina (Compliance): Our compliance lead will want to map events to our control matrix — definitely want to see field names and timestamps.
[00:38] Diego (Redwood SE): Absolutely. At a high level Redwood emits admin_events, api_requests, auth_events, model_inference_events, and system_alerts. Admin_events include GUI actions (user role change, policy edits), CLI/admin API calls, and service-account activities.
[00:52] Samir (SRE): When you say GUI actions, are there user IDs that map back to SSO princ—like an OIDC sub?
[00:58] Diego (Redwood SE): Yes, we attach the principal id we receive from your IdP assertion (usually the OIDC sub or SAML NameID). There's sometimes noise where the assertion doesn't include a stable id, we fall back to email. We log both auth_claims and principal_id so you can map.
[01:15] Priya (CISO): Good. Does the audit include token-level metadata? For example which model prompted tokens, token counts, cost attribution?
[01:22] Hannah (Product): We capture request metadata: model_name, model_version, prompt_hash (optionally obfuscated), token_counts, latency_ms, route_id. For PII-sensitive prompts, we offer a prompt redaction toggle—if on, the prompt field is omitted and only a hashed fingerprint provided.
[01:40] Ethan (Platform): About exports — can you stream raw events to our GCP Pub/Sub? We want near-real-time ingest into our SIEM.
[01:47] Diego (Redwood SE): Yes. We support push to S3 (batched daily/hourly), streaming to Pub/Sub or Kafka, and webhooks. For Pub/Sub we provide a service account + key material handshake or you can configure a connector. Note: streaming has at-least-once semantics; we'll include sequence numbers and monotonic offsets in the payload.
[02:04] Priya (CISO): And encryption in transit and at rest?
[02:07] Diego (Redwood SE): TLS in transit. At rest, if you export to your S3/GCS bucket it's encrypted with your bucket's encryption (you control the CMK). If you use Redwood-hosted export storage we encrypt with Redwood KMS-backed keys. For customer-managed keys, we support envelope encryption where Redwood keeps a short-lived data key encrypted with your CMK.
[02:29] Lina (Compliance): Can you walk through the envelope flow? We've got strict key separation policies.
[02:34] Diego (Redwood SE): Sure — flow: Redwood generates a data key per export chunk, encrypts the payload locally with that data key, then wraps the data key with your CMK via the KMS API (so Redwood never has unencrypted long-term copies). The wrapped key and metadata are stored with the object. On Artemis side, your KMS unwrapping process returns plaintext data key for authorized decrypt.
[02:58] Samir (SRE): How about key rotation? If we rotate CMKs quarterly, can we still decrypt prior exports?
[03:05] Diego (Redwood SE): Yes — the wrapped data key includes key version metadata and we keep a manifest for rewrap operations. If a CMK is scheduled for rotation, you can either rewrap the wrapped keys with the new CMK or keep the old CMK active for decryption-only purposes. We document rewrap steps in the KMS onboarding runbook.
[03:22] Priya (CISO): For SOC2 evidence, we need a tamper-evident snapshot of admin activity. Do you provide an immutable snapshot or WORM-like export?
[03:29] Maya (Redwood AE): We have two patterns: 1) daily signed manifests written to an immutable bucket (object lock enabled) that includes SHA256 checksums and a signing key; 2) streaming to your SIEM where you can apply append-only retention. For legal hold, we can tag exports and extend retention via policy.
[03:46] Lina (Compliance): The signed manifest sounds promising. Who signs it?
[03:50] Diego (Redwood SE): Redwood signs manifest with a rotating signing key. We store the public key in our transparency log. If you prefer, you can require that the manifest be signed by your key via an external signing step after the object lands in your bucket.
[04:05] Ethan (Platform): About payload schema — do you provide a JSON schema and sample payloads? We need to map fields to our control IDs.
[04:11] Hannah (Product): Yes, we'll share sample manifests and a JSON schema. The event payload includes: event_type, timestamp_utc, principal_id, principal_claims, request_id, resource_path, action, outcome, metadata (freeform). We'll also include an event_class for quick grouping.
[04:30] Priya (CISO): How long do Redwood keep raw admin logs on your side by default?
[04:34] Maya (Redwood AE): Hosted default is 90 days for raw events, 365 days for aggregated metrics. If you're on Dedicated or Private you can configure retention and retention policies.
[04:44] Priya (CISO): For our audit we need 7 years retention for certain controls. Can Redwood support long-term export automation?
[04:51] Diego (Redwood SE): Yes — we can automate daily exports to your long-term storage. We recommend lifecycle rules on your bucket to transition to cold storage (e.g., Archive/Coldline) and we can include lifecycle manifests for verification.
[05:05] Samir (SRE): One technical Q: are KV cache invalidation/admin changes part of admin events? We need to know when a cache flush happened because it affects reproducibility of responses.
[05:14] Diego (Redwood SE): Good point — cache ops (kv_cache_evict, kv_cache_warm, model_reload) are emitted as admin_events with target shard and sequence info. We also log model config diffs on deploys so you can correlate inference variance.
[05:29] Ethan (Platform): Any PII handling in logs? We need to avoid capturing raw prompts in logs for certain regs.
[05:34] Hannah (Product): We have redaction toggles. You can choose full prompt redact, partial hash, or include prompt for internal projects. Redaction operates at ingestion time; redacted prompts are replaced with reversible hashes if you enable token-level rehydrate via KMS flows, otherwise it's irreversible.
[05:53] Priya (CISO): Okay. On SSO and RBAC mapping — is role change recorded with pre/post state? We need to show exactly when privileges were escalated.
[06:01] Diego (Redwood SE): Yes, role_change events include before_role and after_role snapshots, who initiated the change, and whether it went through approval workflow (if enabled). Approval workflow actions are also logged.
[06:12] Priya (CISO): For chain-of-custody, can you show us proof that event payloads haven't been modified after export?
[06:18] Diego (Redwood SE): That's the signed manifest plus object checksums. If you want stronger guarantees, we can append a hash to a third-party timestamping service or provide periodic Merkle tree root publishing. We've done that in a few high-compliance pilots.
[06:33] Lina (Compliance): Are those third-party timestamping integrations part of standard offering?
[06:37] Hannah (Product): Not standard, but available as an add-on. We can open an engineering ticket if Artemis needs it in contract.
[06:45] Maya (Redwood AE): Quick pause — any blockers for us to propose a pilot?
[06:50] Priya (CISO): We need a sample export, KMS runbook, SOC2 pack, and manifest schema. Also timeline: pilot for 30 days, export to our S3 bucket, streaming to Pub/Sub for SIEM, and a short regression test.
[07:04] Diego (Redwood SE): We'll prepare a sample export of 7 days of synthetic events so you can validate ingest and schema mapping. We'll also provide instructions for granting Redwood limited kms:Encrypt permissions to wrap keys.
[07:16] Ethan (Platform): For access governance, what's the RBAC model? Do we integrate with SCIM and groups from IdP?
[07:22] Maya (Redwood AE): Yes SCIM provisioning, SAML/OIDC for SSO, and role sync. You can sync groups and map them to Redwood roles. Audit events will include the group membership at time of action.
[07:33] Priya (CISO): Any considerations around data residency? We need events to stay in EU buckets for GDPR controls.
[07:39] Diego (Redwood SE): You can route exports to region-specific destinations; if using Redwood-hosted archival we can ensure EU-only storage options. For hosted processing, metadata may transit outside but we can put strict egress policies in contract or opt for Private deployment where control plane is in your VPC.
[07:56] Lina (Compliance): How do you handle deletion requests under GDPR? Our legal wants proof deletion occurred and the audit trail of the deletion.
[08:03] Diego (Redwood SE): Deletions are recorded as admin_events with redaction and tombstone markers. For exported copies in your bucket, Redwood will provide a deletion manifest for objects we control; for customer-managed buckets you control deletion flow. We can also provide attestations for Redwood-hosted data removals.
[08:19] Maya (Redwood AE): Alright let's recap next steps.
[08:22] Priya (CISO): Quick clarifying Q — do you support immutability locks at object-level via S3 Object Lock?
[08:28] Diego (Redwood SE): If we write to your S3 we can mark objects with Object Lock if the bucket is configured accordingly and your account grants us permission. For Redwood-managed storage, we emulate via signed manifests and internal WORM policies.
[08:42] Maya (Redwood AE): Good. We'll share the following: SOC2 redacted pack link, schema + sample payloads, KMS runbook, and an S3 Pub/Sub configuration checklist. We'll also propose pilot dates.
[08:54] Ethan (Platform): Timeline—can we start pilot week of Nov 22?
[08:58] Maya (Redwood AE): Tentative yes, pending your infra access.
[09:02] Priya (CISO): Thanks everyone.
[09:04] Maya (Redwood AE): Thanks — we'll follow up with artifacts.
[09:07] (end)
